findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector reads exactly argc varargs (networking.c:4158-4173). With argc=6 it consumes hsetex, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field and drops newobj (the value). Every HINCRBYFLOAT replicates as "HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field" with no value, a syntax error on the replica/AOF load, breaking replication for a mainline command and desyncing replica data. The added test expects {hsetex h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1 *} and will fail.
findings.failureMode: Malformed replicated command: replica/AOF gets HSETEX missing the value argument, causing execution error and master-replica data divergence on every HINCRBYFLOAT.
findings.title: rewriteClientCommandVector argc=6 but 7 arguments passed; value dropped from replicated HSETEX

findings.description: Base line was `hashTypeSet(c->db, o,c->argv[2]->ptr,new,HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL);`. The diff removes HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL, so HINCRBYFLOAT on the master now removes the field's expiration (hashTypeSet without KEEP_TTL clears field TTL at t_hash.c:989), while the rewritten replication uses KEEPTTL so a replica would retain it — the exact inconsistency this PR sets out to fix, now inverted, plus TTL loss on master. HINCRBY (line 2506) still uses KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with a TTL silently removes the TTL on the master while the replicated command preserves it: TTL data loss and master/replica divergence.
findings.title: HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL dropped from HINCRBYFLOAT local hashTypeSet — master now deletes field TTL

findings.description: The diff changes `static GetFieldRes addHashFieldToReply(...)` to non-static, but all callers remain in src/t_hash.c (grep shows no other file uses it). AGENTS.md rule 7 requires internal helpers to be static; this exports the symbol needlessly.
findings.failureMode: Mandate violation: symbol pollution; internal helper visible to other compilation units contrary to repository rule 7.
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply loses static despite being file-local (mandate #7)

findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc 6 but 7 robj* arguments (HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, newobj). Only the first 6 are used, so the propagated command is "HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field" without the value. Replicas fail the command (numfields 1 but no value pair → arity/syntax error) causing master/replica divergence, and an AOF containing this malformed command aborts on reload. Upstream fix uses argc 7. Fix: change 6 to 7.
findings.failureMode: Malformed HSETEX propagated to replicas/AOF: replica errors and diverges; AOF reload fails
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT replicated with argc=6, dropping the value argument

findings.description: Base had `hashTypeSet(c->db, o,c->argv[2]->ptr,new,HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL);`. The diff removes HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL, so HINCRBYFLOAT on the master now clears the field's expiration — the very bug class this PR fixes on the replica. E.g. HSETEX h EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1; HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1 → HTTL returns -1 on master while replica (via KEEPTTL propagation) keeps the TTL, causing master/replica divergence. HINCRBY (unchanged) still passes HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL. Fix: restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT removes field TTL on master; master/replica TTL inconsistency
findings.title: HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL dropped from HINCRBYFLOAT hashTypeSet on master

findings.description: The diff removes the `static` qualifier from addHashFieldToReply, but all uses remain inside src/t_hash.c (lines 2605, 2621, 2685, 2810). This violates the repository mandate that internal helper functions be declared static, exporting an unnecessary symbol. Fix: restore `static`.
findings.failureMode: Mandate 7 violation: non-static internal helper pollutes global symbol namespace
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply loses static despite being file-local

findings.description: New endpoint uses `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")`. RolesGuard's hasMinimumRole treats TEAM_MEMBER as the lowest bar, so any plain team member can generate invite links, contradicting the PR contract ("Requires TEAM_ADMIN role") and the PR's own e2e test which expects 403 for a MEMBER (`should fail to create invite as non-admin member`). Consequence: authorization gap letting non-admin members mint tokens that grant team membership, plus a failing e2e test.
findings.failureMode: Non-admin member POSTs /v2/teams/:teamId/invite and receives 200 with a valid invite token, an authorization bypass relative to the intended admin-only surface; e2e test expecting 403 fails.
findings.title: Invite endpoint gated at TEAM_MEMBER instead of TEAM_ADMIN

findings.description: Changed `token,` to `token: newToken.identifier`, so createInvite now returns the constant string `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>` instead of the random hex token. Every caller (new v2 endpoint, existing org-teams invite controller, tRPC createInvite handler) receives a useless "token" that cannot be redeemed; the PR's own e2e assertions (`inviteLink toContain(token)`, tokens differ per request) fail because the identifier is constant and never appears in the link.
findings.failureMode: API responses expose the identifier string as the invite token; consumers who use the returned token (e.g. tRPC clients passing it back via options.token, or users sharing the token) get NotFound / invalid-invite errors.
findings.title: createInvite returns verification identifier instead of token

findings.description: Base code was `if (!isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink;`. The diff flips it to `if (isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink;`, so organizations/sub-teams now get the plain `${WEBAPP_URL}/teams?token=` link while regular standalone teams get the `/signup?token=...&callbackUrl=...` org link. This regresses the existing web MemberInvitationModal and org-teams invite v2 endpoint: invited users land on the wrong flow (org invitees skip signup/onboarding path; regular team invitees are sent to signup instead of /teams).
findings.failureMode: Wrong invite URL returned for both org and non-org contexts on the mainline invite flow.
findings.title: buildInviteLink org/team condition inverted

findings.description: New import `@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService` is the only direct `@calcom/features` import in all of apps/api/v2/src; every other v2 consumer (e.g. OrganizationsTeamsInviteController) imports `TeamService` from `@calcom/platform-libraries`, which is prebuilt by `build:docker`/`dev:build`. apps/api/v2/package.json does not depend on @calcom/features and its tsconfig lacks path mappings for the transitive aliases the features source needs, so building/type-checking api v2 would need to compile the raw uncompiled features graph and is expected to fail.
findings.failureMode: apps/api/v2 build/type-check (and docker build which only prebuilds platform-* packages) fails resolving/compiling the uncompiled @calcom/features source graph.
findings.title: API v2 controller imports TeamService from @calcom/features source instead of @calcom/platform-libraries

findings.description: write_and_make_executable returns Result<(), FileWriteError> but callers in prepare_tools (crate::Result) use `?`; no From<FileWriteError> exists on crate::Error.
findings.failureMode: cargo build fails: From<FileWriteError> not implemented for Error.
findings.title: FileWriteError not convertible to crate::Error — compile failure

findings.description: Base had `if !gtk.exists()`; head has `if gtk.exists()`. On a fresh machine the linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh file is never created, yet linuxdeploy is always invoked with `--plugin gtk`, so AppImage bundling fails (plugin not found). Defeats the purpose of the PR.

findings.title: Inverted condition: GTK plugin script only written when it already exists

findings.failureMode: Fresh tools dir: set_permissions on missing file -> NotFound -> bundling aborts.
findings.title: set_permissions before fs::write fails on nonexistent file

findings.description: Base downloaded `linuxdeploy-{linuxdeploy_arch}.AppImage` (i686 -> i383). Head downloads `linuxdeploy-{arch}.AppImage` while still saving to a `{linuxdeploy_arch}`-named file. If the release asset follows the linuxdeploy_arch naming, the i686 download 404s and bundling fails on 32-bit x86.
findings.failureMode: i686 target: download URL differs from asset name -> HTTP 404 -> prepare_tools errors.
findings.title: linuxdeploy download URL uses {arch} instead of {linuxdeploy_arch}

findings.failureMode: Mandate violation: manual Display/Error instead of thiserror.

Elsewhere the org variant (organizations-teams-invite.controller.ts) uses @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN"). Fix: use @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").
findings.failureMode: Non-admin team member calls POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite and successfully creates an invite link (authorization gap); e2e test "should fail to create invite as non-admin member" fails.

findings.title: buildInviteLink condition inverted

BVC's handleDisplayActions runs toggleReaderModeLongPressAction() for that case instead of toggleReaderMode(), so tapping the reader mode toolbar button triggers the add-to-reading-list long-press behavior instead of toggling reader mode.

findings.title: showReaderMode now maps to .readerModeLongPressAction display view

findings.title: Toolbar leading anchored to wrong skeleton bar → unsatisfiable constraints

When trailing page actions exist but leading ones don't (or vice versa), dividerWidthConstraint gets the wrong constant, producing wrong divider/spacing layout in the address bar.

findings.title: Divider width keyed to wrong stack (leading instead of trailing page actions)

findings.title: Unused isLandscape variable with misleading comment

Newly added buttons get alpha 0 in updateActionStack and are only restored via `stacks`; trailing page action buttons (reload/share/reader mode) remain invisible after toolbar reconfiguration.

This forces toolbar.width = -(rightSkeleton width), an unsatisfiable/negative constraint. With swiping tabs enabled the auto layout engine breaks constraints and the address toolbar collapses or is mispositioned.

findings.title: Toolbar leading anchored to rightSkeletonAddressBar, producing negative-width toolbar

The rename changed it to `leadingPageActionStack`. When trailing page actions exist but leading ones don't (or vice versa), the divider width is wrong: divider hidden while trailing actions are shown, or shown with no trailing actions.

findings.description: The diff flips `"strict": true` to `"strict": false` in tsconfig.app.json. Repository mandate 11 requires strict type checking in the validation pipeline (validate:types runs `tsc -b --noEmit`). This change disables strictNullChecks/noImplicitAny etc. for every file in the app, so real type errors (including nullability bugs in the new trigger components, e.g. `field.value?.[0]` on union-typed fields) no longer fail validation and can ship to production. This is a diff-visible weakening of an enforcement mechanism, explicitly findings-eligible.
findings.failureMode: Type errors across the frontend pass CI type validation; latent null/undefined and shape bugs reach production; violates mandate 11.
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled for entire ui-v2 app

findings.description: DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and the pre-existing FlowRunStateTriggerFields both switch the status field to `trigger.after` when posture is Proactive. WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields and WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields hardcode `name="trigger.expect"` regardless of posture, so a Proactive work-pool/work-queue trigger stores the selected status in `expect` with an empty `after`, producing a different (wrong) trigger payload than the identical deployment/flow-run pattern. A user creating a Proactive work-pool automation gets a trigger that expects the status event within the window rather than one keyed off the status via `after`, i.e. semantics diverge from all sibling templates. Same fix applies at work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx line 36.
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-pool/work-queue automations are created with the status in the wrong trigger field, yielding wrong automation behavior.
findings.title: Work pool/queue status fields write Proactive selection to trigger.expect instead of trigger.after

findings.description: `e.target.value.split("\n")` always returns at least one element, so `lines.length > 0` is always true and the `undefined` branch is unreachable. Clearing the textarea sets `trigger.expect` to `[""]` (and blank interior lines produce empty-string entries), so the submitted custom trigger contains an empty-string event name instead of an unset/empty expect. Fix: filter empty lines and pass undefined when none remain.
findings.failureMode: Automation created with expect: [""] (empty event name) after user clears the textarea; trigger never matches / invalid payload.
findings.title: Custom trigger textarea can never clear expect; empty text yields [""]

findings.description: The diff flips "strict": true to "strict": false in tsconfig.app.json, unrelated to the trigger form feature. Mandate #11 requires strict mode with validate:types (tsc -b --noEmit, package.json line 19). With strict off, null/undefined and implicit-any errors across the whole ui-v2 app pass validate:types, so CI type checking no longer catches whole classes of defects.

findings.description: DeploymentStatusTriggerFields switches the status field to trigger.after when posture is Proactive, while the two status siblings added in this PR always use trigger.expect. A Proactive deployment trigger then has after=[status] and no expect, which per Prefect proactive semantics (docs event-triggers.mdx: proactive triggers fire when the "expect" events are not seen) fires on the absence of ANY event rather than the selected status. Also, a status chosen in Reactive mode remains stale in trigger.expect after switching to Proactive, so both fields can end up populated with contradictory values.
findings.failureMode: Proactive deployment-status automation is created with empty expect / stale expect+after, firing on wrong conditions
findings.title: Deployment status Proactive mode writes status to trigger.after, diverging from work-pool/work-queue siblings and leaving expect empty

findings.description: String.split("\n") always returns at least one element, so `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` is always `lines`. Clearing the textarea stores trigger.expect = [""], and blank lines yield empty-string entries. findings.description: escape_like_pattern escapes with backslash (e.g. "test_data" -> "test\\_data"), but the SQL declares ESCAPE '|'. The backslash is therefore a literal character: a search for "test_data" produces pattern %test\_data% which no longer matches documents containing "test_data" (backslash literal, underscore still a wildcard needing a preceding char). Queries containing %, _ or \ return wrong/empty results; a query containing '|' followed by a char forms an invalid/unintended escape sequence. The escape char must be '\\' (or the helper parameterized).
findings.failureMode: Full-text fallback search on IRIS (IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled) returns wrong/no results for queries containing _, %, or \, and may error on '|' input
findings.title: IRIS LIKE fallback declares ESCAPE '|' but pattern is backslash-escaped

findings.description: The SQL text emitted is ESCAPE '\\' (two backslash characters inside the literal). If ClickZetta parses string literals ANSI-style (as the existing '' quote-doubling in this file implies), the escape string is two characters -> SQL error on every LIKE fallback search. If ClickZetta parses backslash escapes (Spark/MySQL style), the interpolated pattern's \% / \_ sequences are consumed by the literal parser, so escaping is ineffective and a query containing a literal backslash yields an invalid trailing-escape pattern -> query error. Either way the intended escaping does not work as written.
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta LIKE fallback search errors or silently keeps wildcard behavior for special-character queries
findings.title: ClickZetta LIKE fallback: ESCAPE '\\\\' / backslash interpolation into string literal is dialect-inconsistent

findings.description: Loop `for (int j = 0; j <= keys_result->numkeys; j++)` iterates one past the last key (base used `j < numkeys`). At j==numkeys it reads keys[numkeys] (out of bounds of the heap keys array when numkeys > MAX_KEYS_BUFFER, and a stale/zero entry otherwise), dereferences argv[garbage pos], and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] one int past the malloc'd buffer (heap corruption). Concrete mainline failure: in cluster mode, `GET foo` yields keys={pos=1}; iteration j=1 hashes argv[0] ("GET") as a key, its slot almost never matches foo's slot, so the function returns CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT and preprocessCommand marks CLIENT_READ_CROSS_SLOT — every single-slot command is rejected with a cross-slot error; for multi-key heap-allocated results the OOB read of keys[numkeys].pos can index argv with garbage and crash. Fix: `j < keys_result->numkeys`.

findings.failureMode: Untracked memory allocation on the per-command hot path; mandate violation
findings.title: Direct malloc/free in extractSlotFromKeysResult violates zmalloc mandate; buffer is dead weight

findings.description: escape_like_pattern escapes %, _ and \ using backslash, but the SQL declares `ESCAPE '|'`. The escape characters therefore do not match: a query like "test_data" becomes pattern `%test\_data%`, where `\` is a literal char and `_` remains a wildcard, so it no longer matches stored text "test_data" (requires a literal backslash). Queries containing %/_/\ return wrong or empty results, and the intended wildcard-injection prevention is not achieved. Fix: use `ESCAPE '\'` (backslash) to match the escaping helper, or escape with '|'.
findings.failureMode: Full-text fallback search on IRIS returns wrong/no results for queries containing _, % or \; wildcard escaping ineffective
findings.title: IRIS LIKE fallback escapes with backslash but declares ESCAPE '|'

findings.description: Base code built the keyword as `keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')` with `\\u` doubling so that non-ASCII keywords (e.g. Chinese) match WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs, which are stored via json.dumps with default ensure_ascii=True (see sqlalchemy_workflow_execution_repository.py:152 `db_model.inputs = json.dumps(domain_model.inputs)`), i.e. non-ASCII text is persisted as \\uXXXX escapes. The new code searches the raw keyword, which never appears in the ASCII-escaped JSON, so keyword search for any non-ASCII term now returns zero results. The escaping fix needs to be composed with the unicode_escape transformation, not replace it.
findings.failureMode: Workflow app log keyword search returns no results for non-ASCII keywords
findings.title: Dropped unicode_escape encoding breaks non-ASCII keyword search in workflow logs

findings.description: The code writes `ESCAPE '\\\\'` (SQL text `ESCAPE '\\'`), which only denotes a single-character backslash escape if ClickZetta string literals themselves use backslash escaping. But the pattern literal `'%{escaped_query}%'` embeds escape_like_pattern output without that same doubling. Under the same literal-parsing convention, a query containing a backslash (escape_like_pattern → `\\`) is collapsed back to a single `\` inside the literal, which then acts as the ESCAPE character and escapes the following content character — e.g. searching "a\b" yields pattern `%a\b%`, matching "ab" instead of "a\b". Conversely, if ClickZetta literals are standard-conforming (no backslash escapes), `ESCAPE '\\'` is a two-character escape string and the query errors. Either way the LIKE fallback misbehaves for inputs containing backslashes. Fix: apply the same doubling to the pattern's backslashes as to the ESCAPE literal (or use a non-backslash escape char).
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta LIKE fallback search returns wrong results or errors for queries containing backslashes
findings.title: ClickZetta LIKE pattern backslashes not doubled consistently with ESCAPE literal

findings.description: The "contains", "start with" and "end with" branches pass escape="\\" to like(), but the "not contains" branch calls `json_field.notlike(f"%{escaped_value}%")` without the escape parameter. The value is still backslash-escaped by escape_like_pattern, so no ESCAPE clause is emitted and, on backends where backslash is not the default LIKE escape character, the escaped sequence `\%`/`\_` is treated as two literal characters — e.g. "not contains 50%" then wrongly fails to exclude documents whose metadata contains "50%". Fix: add escape="\\" like the sibling branches.
findings.failureMode: Wrong metadata filtering results for "not contains" with special characters
findings.title: "not contains" metadata filter missing escape="\\" on notlike

findings.description: Repository mandate 16 requires snake_case for Python variables. The new helper uses `escapedPattern` (camelCase). Should be `escaped_pattern`.
findings.failureMode: Naming-convention mandate violation on changed line
findings.title: camelCase variable `escapedPattern` violates snake_case mandate

findings.description: Loop `for (int j = 0; j <= keys_result->numkeys; j++)` iterates one past the end. It writes slot_buffer[numkeys] (heap buffer of numkeys ints -> OOB write on every keyed command) and reads keys[numkeys].pos. For a single-key command like GET foo in cluster mode, keys[1] is the zeroed keysbuf entry, pos=0 -> argv[0] ("GET") is hashed as a key, mismatching foo's slot -> function returns CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT, so preprocessCommand marks CLIENT_READ_CROSS_SLOT for virtually every single-key command. When keys are heap-allocated (>6 keys), keys[numkeys].pos is uninitialized -> argv[garbage] OOB read/crash. Fix: `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Heap out-of-bounds write/read plus wrong CROSSSLOT result rejecting mainline single-key commands in cluster mode
findings.title: Off-by-one loop in extractSlotFromKeysResult: heap overflow and false CROSSSLOT on every keyed command

findings.description: New code calls `malloc(sizeof(int) * keys_result->numkeys)` and `free(slot_buffer)` directly. Repository mandate #2 requires zmalloc/zfree outside the zmalloc implementation. Consequence: allocation bypasses Redis memory tracking (used_memory/maxmemory accounting) and, unlike zmalloc, an OOM returns NULL which is dereferenced unchecked at slot_buffer[j], a reachable crash under memory pressure.
findings.failureMode: Untracked allocation and unchecked malloc NULL deref crash under OOM; mandate violation
findings.title: Direct malloc/free in extractSlotFromKeysResult violates zmalloc mandate

findings.description: The new guard `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` explicitly lets None through, so `render_template` (declared `-> str`) returns None when the executor result lacks a "result" key or maps it to None (e.g. any injected/custom code_executor, which this abstraction exists to support). `_run` then executes `len(rendered)` and crashes with an unhandled TypeError instead of raising TemplateRenderError / returning a FAILED NodeRunResult. Fix: treat None as invalid in the guard.

findings.description: The guard `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` deliberately lets None through, so `return rendered` has type `str | None` against declared `-> str`. basedpyright strict (run by style.yml via dev/basedpyright-check on changed files) fails: "Type \"str | None\" is not assignable to return type \"str\" (reportReturnType)". If None ever escaped, _run would crash with TypeError on len(rendered) instead of returning a FAILED result. Fix: raise TemplateRenderError when rendered is not a str (drop the None exemption).
findings.failureMode: Required CI type-check job fails deterministically on this new file, blocking the merge; latent TypeError path if result lacks "result" key.
